chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abd Salih (peace be upon him)
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on zakat for owned and contracted slaves according to Imam Musa ibn al-Kadhim?
ai.summary: This brief narration from al-Kafi serves as a corroborative link in the chain of transmission, confirming the legal ruling on zakat for owned and contracted slaves as established in the preceding hadith. By stating 'similar to it,' the 7th Imam, Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), reinforces the consistency of this fiscal obligation within Shia jurisprudence, ensuring that the wealth of slaves is subject to the same purification and almsgiving requirements as other assets. This repetition underscores the importance of clarity in financial obligations for different categories of property in early Islamic society.
